newsitem.title: CANADA: POLYGRAM'S CANADA FILM PROPOSAL OPPOSED.
newsitem.headline: POLYGRAM'S CANADA FILM PROPOSAL OPPOSED.

text.p: The official opposition in Canada's Parliament urged the Liberal government on Wednesday to block PolyGram NV from distributing independent movies in Canada.
"(Industry) Minister John Manley must turn down this request," said Gaston Leroux, spokesman on cultural matters for the separatist Bloc Quebecois, in a statement.

The Dutch company's PolyGram Filmed Entertainment unit is seeking exemption from strict rules intended to protect Canadian film distributors and producers, promising in return to invest heavily in the Canadian film industry.
Manley told reporters he was required to make a decision on the application, with input from Canadian Heritage Minister Sheila Copps. He declined to say when a decision was expected.
PolyGram, 75 percent owned by Philips Electronics NV , has trumpeted its success in backing non-U.S. films such as "Trainspotting."

According to media reports, PolyGram is pledging to reinvest 20 percent of its Canadian revenues in the domestic film industry during the five years. In return, the company is seeking the rights to distribute the resulting Canadian films in other countries.

"Those movies constitute the basic revenues of Canadian distributors who in turn reinvest part of their profits in Canadian productions," said Leroux of Polygram's plans to offer independent movies in Canada:
"Any exemption granted to a company such as PolyGram would weaken the Canadian movie industry. It would lead to more requests of the kind," he said.
PolyGram contends that the country's cultural restrictions have failed to foster a strong Canadian film industry.
